transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brought me in is my eating has been getting kind of out of hand, especially after my evening class. I’ll tell myself I’m just going to stop and grab something quick because I didn’t eat much during the day, or I’m tired, or it’s late, but then it turns into a lot more than that.

Like I might get a full fast-food meal, and then I’ll end up getting candy from the vending machine too, and by the time I get home I’m still eating—chips or crackers or whatever snacks are around. It feels like I’m trying to make up for the whole day all at once, even though I know that sounds strange. I’m 55 years old, I work in bookkeeping, and I feel like I should have a better handle on this, but it’s been happening enough that I’m embarrassed and figured I should talk to someone.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate or control your weight?

Yeah… I’m embarrassed to say this, but yes, a few times. Not every time it happens, but after some of those late-night eating spells, I’ve gone into the bathroom and made myself throw up.

It’s usually when I’m sitting there afterward feeling kind of panicky, like I can almost picture all that food turning into weight on me right away, or like it’s going to show on my stomach or my face or something. I know that probably doesn’t sound rational, but in the moment it feels really urgent, like I have to undo it somehow. So I’ve made myself vomit a few times because I was scared of what all the food would do to me.
Do these episodes of overeating usually happen when you're alone, and do you feel like you can't stop yourself once you start eating?

Yeah… it’s usually when I’m by myself, or at least when no one’s really paying attention to me. And the not being able to stop part is… that’s probably the thing that scares me the most.

Like I’ll start with something that seems normal, like a bag of chips or crackers, and I’ll literally tell myself, “Okay, just have some and then close the bag and go to bed.” I’ll even fold the top over sometimes, like I’m done. But then a minute later my hand is back in it again. It’s like I’m having this argument in my head the whole time—“Stop now, you’re going to feel awful, just put it away”—but my hands just keep reaching for more anyway.

And then after a while I’m not even enjoying it, really. I’m just eating because I’ve already started, if that makes sense. By the end I feel embarrassed and kind of sick of myself, like, “Why couldn’t I just stop when I said I would?” So yes, I guess I do feel out of control once it gets going.
Has this eating behavior caused you a lot of distress or affected your daily life, like making it hard to focus on work or enjoy time with others?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still functioning, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely fallen apart, because I do still get my bookkeeping work done, and I’ve been keeping up with my classwork too. I’m not missing deadlines or anything like that, at least not so far.

But it has changed how I act around people. After my evening class, I used to maybe hang around for a few minutes, talk with classmates, ask about an assignment, that kind of thing. Nothing major, just normal casual conversation. Now I find myself packing up really fast and leaving almost as soon as class ends. I’ll tell myself I’m just tired or I need to get home, but honestly a lot of it is that I feel ashamed and preoccupied. I’m thinking about getting home, or what I might eat, or I’m already feeling bad about the whole pattern.

So it hasn’t stopped me from doing the basic responsibilities, but it’s made me more withdrawn. I don’t really enjoy that time with classmates anymore because I’m so in my head about it.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of these eating episodes?

I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless, exactly. I mean, I get upset with myself after the eating happens, and I can feel pretty low in that moment, but outside of that… I don’t know if I’d call it being depressed.

I still do my usual things, more or less. It’s not like everything feels pointless or like I can’t get out of bed or anything. I do feel kind of preoccupied, and maybe less social than I used to be, but that feels tied to the eating stuff and the shame around it more than some separate, all-day sadness.

As far as losing interest in things I usually enjoy… I guess I haven’t really noticed that in a clear way. I still can enjoy things when I’m not in my head about all this. So… no, not really, or at least not in a way I could separate from the eating episodes themselves.
How often do these episodes of overeating followed by feeling out of control happen? Do they occur regularly, like at least once a week for several weeks?

Yeah… it has been regular. I don’t know why it feels hard to say it that plainly, but it’s not just a one-off thing.

For about the last three months, there’s usually been at least one night each week where it happens, mostly after my class. I’ll get home and overeat in that way where I feel like I’ve lost control, and then afterward I make myself throw up. Some weeks it’s just that one night, but it’s been consistent enough that I’ve started almost expecting it, which makes me feel awful to admit.

So yes… at least once a week for several weeks. More like around three months.

Outside of feeling preoccupied or withdrawing from social time after class, have these eating episodes caused you any other problems in your daily life, like difficulties at work, with family, or in other important areas?

Not really in a big obvious way, no. I mean, I still get my bookkeeping work done. I go in, I do what I’m supposed to do, I keep track of the numbers, I finish the tasks. And with my coursework, I’m still turning things in and showing up to class. So if someone looked at me from the outside, they might think, “Well, he’s managing.”

But it has affected things around class more than I’d like to admit. I’ve started leaving really quickly afterward, like almost as soon as it ends. I used to stay a little, talk to people, maybe ask a question or just have normal small talk. Now I pack up and get out of there because I feel ashamed and distracted, and I’m already thinking about getting home. It’s like my mind is not really there with the people around me.

So I wouldn’t say it’s caused major problems at work or with responsibilities, but it’s definitely made me more avoidant socially after class. I don’t like that part.
